title: A simultaneous perturbation preserves the Artin-Rees bound for the right differential
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal contained in every maximal ideal of $A$. Let $L,M,N$ be finitely generated $A$-modules, and let $f,f':L\to M$ and $g,g':M\to N$ be $A$-linear maps with $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$ and $g'f'=0$. For a module $T$, write $I^nT$ for the submodule generated by products $ax$ with $a\in I^n$ and $x\in T$, with $I^0=A$. Suppose an integer $c\geq0$ satisfies, for every $n\geq c$, $$\operatorname{im}f\cap I^nM\subseteq f(I^{n-c}L),\qquad \operatorname{im}g\cap I^nN\subseteq g(I^{n-c}M).$$ Assume also $(f-f')(L)\subseteq I^{c+1}M$ and $(g-g')(M)\subseteq I^{c+1}N$. Then, for every $n\geq c$, $$\operatorname{im}g'\cap I^nN\subseteq g'(I^{n-c}M).$$

source.place: Tag 07VE (lemma-approximate-complex), first conclusion and first paragraph of the proof: preservation of the Artin-Rees bound for the right differential; no use of the additional exactness conclusion.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq c$ and $y\in\operatorname{im}g'\cap I^nN$. Choose $a_0\in M$ with $g'(a_0)=y$, and put $k=n-c$. We construct, by induction for $0\leq r\leq k$, elements $a_r\in I^rM$ with $g'(a_r)=y$. The chosen $a_0$ supplies the base case because $I^0M=M$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first paragraph of proof; finite adjustment argument, part 1.

proof.text: For any linear map $u:T\to U$ with $u(T)\subseteq I^{c+1}U$, linearity gives $u(I^sT)\subseteq I^{s+c+1}U$: write an element of $I^sT$ as a finite sum $\sum_j\alpha_jx_j$ with $\alpha_j\in I^s$, and expand $u(\sum_j\alpha_jx_j)=\sum_j\alpha_ju(x_j)$. Each term $\alpha_ju(x_j)$ lies in $I^s(I^{c+1}U)=(I^sI^{c+1})U=I^{s+c+1}U$. We apply this to $g-g'$ and $f-f'$ below.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first paragraph of proof; finite adjustment argument, part 2.

proof.text: Suppose $0\leq r<k$ and $a_r$ has been constructed. Then $r+c+1\leq n$, so $I^nN\subseteq I^{r+c+1}N$. Step 2 and $g'(a_r)=y$ give $g(a_r)=y+(g-g')(a_r)\in I^{r+c+1}N$. The assumed bound for $g$, at exponent $r+c+1\geq c$, supplies $e\in I^{r+1}M$ with $g(e)=g(a_r)$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first paragraph of proof; finite adjustment argument, part 3.

proof.text: The equality $g(a_r-e)=0$ and $\ker g=\operatorname{im}f$ give $b\in L$ with $f(b)=a_r-e\in I^rM$. If $r\geq c$, the assumed bound for $f$ at exponent $r$ allows replacing $b$ by an element of $I^{r-c}L$ having the same image. If $r<c$, retain the original $b$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first paragraph of proof; finite adjustment argument, part 4.

proof.text: Put $a_{r+1}=a_r-f'(b)=e+(f-f')(b)$. When $r<c$, the last summand lies in $I^{c+1}M\subseteq I^{r+1}M$. When $r\geq c$, Step 2 puts it in $I^{(r-c)+(c+1)}M=I^{r+1}M$. Thus $a_{r+1}\in I^{r+1}M$; moreover $g'(a_{r+1})=g'(a_r)-g'f'(b)=y$ since $g'f'=0$. This completes the inductive step.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first paragraph of proof; finite adjustment argument, part 5.

proof.text: Finite induction reaches $r=k=n-c$ and gives $y=g'(a_k)\in g'(I^{n-c}M)$. If $n=c$, the induction has no steps and the initial preimage already lies in $I^0M$. Since $n$ and $y$ were arbitrary, the asserted inclusion holds for every $n\geq c$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first paragraph of proof; finite adjustment argument, part 6.
